A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same parallel Picard algorithms and sampling problems. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C support comparison despite changes in title, theoretical scope, and layout.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms and theoretical convergence guarantees, including proof appendices. Its figures and tables present theoretical comparisons and an algorithm schematic, not original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v3 likewise contains theoretical analysis and proofs, with no original experimental, simulation-run, user-study, or data-analysis results in the main text or appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain diagonal updates across time slices, repeated inner Picard iterations for Langevin sampling, and the exponential integrator with early stopping for diffusion sampling. Pseudocode restructuring and expanded explanations do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation scenarios. Both study Langevin sampling and diffusion-model sampling theoretically; the stronger distributional assumption changes theoretical scope rather than evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. After matching updated citations, theoretical Tables 1–2 retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, training budgets, evaluation metrics, or testing procedures. Revised theoretical parameter conditions do not constitute changes to an experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version contains original ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies. The new processor-count and Lipschitz discussions are theoretical qualifications rather than additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, or related uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: No measured performance values or empirical findings are added, removed, or revised. Tables 1–2 retain the headline asymptotic rates for the same methods; changes concern theoretical assumptions and guarantees.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.2 replaces the log-Sobolev assumption with strong log-concavity, substantially restricting its guarantee. New remarks state finite-processor and Lipschitz-dependent complexity bounds, and Appendix C.3.1 adds log(1/η) ≲ T. Appendix A removes the f-divergence theorem and revises the Novikov-condition definition; C.2.1 replaces the detailed Girsanov application with a citation.

C1.justification: v1 claims faster sampling under isoperimetry and matching a lower bound for exponentially small accuracy. v3 restricts the sampling contribution to strongly log-concave targets and removes the optimality/lower-bound-matching assertions. The logarithmic dimension dependence and diffusion-sampling contribution remain.

C2.justification: New Remarks 4.5–4.6 and 5.6–5.7 substantially qualify the efficiency claims: improving condition-number dependence remains open, limited processors can eliminate the advantage, and large score Lipschitz constants increase the required iteration depth. v3 also acknowledges that uniform Lipschitzness may fail near the data endpoint.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3.1 newly specifies log(1/η) ≲ T in the parameter prescription. Conversely, C.1 drops v1's explicit stopping relation t_N = T − η and its O(√η) Wasserstein-error guidance. These are changes to parameter documentation; neither version supplies implementation measurements or code/data access.

R1.justification: The comparison with Zhou, Wang and Sugiyama (2024), central to v1's optimality positioning, and its reference are removed. v3 instead emphasizes improved upper bounds under stronger assumptions and adds connections to finite-resource parallel MCMC, diffusion inference, and Lipschitz singularities in Remarks 4.5–5.7.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, 'iteration complexity' becomes 'adaptive complexity', and selected technical explanations are expanded. Appendix C consolidates existing material into revised subsections and gains a roadmap. The main section sequence and most proof text remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column conference layout. Tables 1–2 are reformatted with highlighted proposed-method rows and assumption markers. v1's lower-bound comparison Figure 1 is removed, while its algorithm schematic Figure 2 is retained as v3's Figure 1; both pseudocode displays are reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important mismatch: Theorem 4.2 now assumes strong log-concavity, consistent with the gradient-contraction argument already used in Appendix B.2, rather than claiming the guarantee under LSI alone. Removing optimality assertions and explaining processor and score-regularity limitations further improves reliability. The narrower scope and shortened appendix explanations are outweighed by this correction to a principal guarantee.
